rgb: The camera wearer is positioned behind a black L-shaped service counter, looking down at the countertop approximately 0.4 to 0.8 metres away. On the counter within arm's reach, from left to right, sit a white touchscreen POS terminal oriented toward the wearer, a small black receipt printer and smartphone, a metal holder filled with wrapped straws, a pump bottle and closed laptop on a lower section to the right, and a bouquet of pink and red flowers roughly 1.0 metre away at the far right. Both have their torsos turned toward the counter and wearer, with their heads cropped above the frame's top edge. Between frames 1 and 5, the viewpoint tilts farther downward and drifts slightly left toward the POS terminal, revealing green-lit equipment beneath the counter at the lower left while pushing the bouquet and most of both people's torsos beyond the top and right frame boundaries. In frame 3, an arm reaches forward from the opposite side of the counter to roughly 0.6 metres from the wearer, meeting the wearer's outstretched right hand beside the terminal. depth: The depth map presents an overhead egocentric view of a service counter located 0.4–0.9 m below and ahead of the camera wearer. A raised point-of-sale (POS) monitor occupies the left, while a receipt printer, straw holder, sanitizer bottle, and closed laptop lie to the right; a flower bouquet appears at the upper right in frames 1–3. In frames 1–2, two people stand beyond the counter at a distance of about 1.0–1.5 m, one dressed in dark blue on the left and one in beige roughly 0.4 m to the right. Their bodies face the counter and camera wearer, and their heads are cut off by the frame's upper edge. Throughout the 5 frames, the wearer angles the camera downward and slightly left toward the counter. At the same time, the wearer's forearms, visible 0.3–0.5 m away along the bottom, and the customer's arm reaching from across the counter enter the central work area within mutual arm's reach to pass cash during frames 3–5, while the second person and bouquet disappear from view. Relative to the dark counter in RGB, the depth map more clearly conveys the 3D height of the angled POS display and tall flower arrangement, as well as the overlapping hand planes during the exchange. Nevertheless, it is unreliable in frames 1–2 because the bouquet receives excessively bright near-depth values similar to the foreground monitor, and in frame 4 because the lower-left counter area blooms too brightly compared with the hands.
segmentation: The segmentation map separates prominent foreground subjects within the counter scene. In frames 1–2, it detects the two people standing across the counter about 1.0–1.5 m away at the upper left and upper center, facing the counter with their heads outside the frame. It also follows the arms and hands reaching from both the camera wearer at the bottom, 0.3–0.5 m away, and the customer at the top, approximately 0.6–0.8 m away, as they come together centrally in frames 3–5. Several counter objects located within the wearer's 0.4–0.8 m reach are also segmented, including the left-side POS terminal, the neighboring receipt printer, the closed laptop at the lower right in frame 1, and the flower arrangement at the upper right in frame 2. Across the sequence, the masks represent the positional change as the background people exit through the upper frame and both of the wearer's arms extend upward from the bottom to meet the customer's outstretched hand near the POS display in frames 3 and 5. During the frame 3 handoff, the map distinctly assigns the touching customer and wearer hands to separate person instances despite their close overlap in RGB. Its object labels and temporal continuity are highly unreliable, however: the POS monitor and receipt printer are incorrectly classified as 'cell phone', the laptop as 'book', and the tiled floor as 'keyboard'. It also fails to capture the bouquet and laptop in most frames and combines the POS screen and printer into one mask in frame 3.
pose: Against a black background, the pose map displays sparse 2D skeletal landmarks, using yellow for body limbs and magenta for hands. It records partial features of the people beyond the counter approximately 1.0–1.5 m away, along with the hands meeting above the counter at distances of 0.3–0.7 m. In frames 1–2, the map identifies a hand and incomplete arm beside the upper-left person's waist, as well as the camera wearer's right hand entering from the bottom in frame 2. It places the customer's reaching hand in the center during frame 3, then follows both wearer hands along the bottom in frames 4–5 and the customer's extended hand positioned above them in frame 5. The magenta finger joints depict the customer's hand pointing downward toward the wearer in frame 5, while the wearer's fingers and palms turn upward and inward within 0.1–0.2 m of that hand. Where the hands are detected in frames 4 and 5, the skeletal wireframe reveals precise finger articulation and palm direction more clearly than the motion-blurred RGB imagery. Even so, the pose map remains very incomplete and unreliable: it omits the torsos and arms of both standing people whose heads are outside the frame, does not detect the wearer's reaching hand in frame 3, and invents small yellow body-skeleton pieces around the hands and counter in frames 1, 3, and 4.
